newsitem.title: USA: RAINS FAIL TO IMPROVE KANSAS CROP RATINGS IN WEEK.
newsitem.headline: RAINS FAIL TO IMPROVE KANSAS CROP RATINGS IN WEEK.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ending August 10. Scattered showers did not improve row crop conditions, according to Kansas Agricultural Statistics and the Kansas State University Extension Service. Although conditions did not improve, crop development progress is ahead of schedule. Corn condition is reported as 16 percent excellent, 48 percent good, 27 percent fair, 8 percent poor, and 1 percent very poor(see table 1). Virtually all of the crop has silked. This is behind 1996 at 100 percent, but ahead of the average of 95 percent. Currently, 60 percent of the corn is in the dough stage. This compares to 76 percent last year and the average of 51 percent. Twenty percent of the crop is dented. This is behind 1996, at 28 percent, but ahead of the average at 14 percent. Sorghum condition is reported as 13 percent excellent, 56 percent good, 25 percent fair, 5 percent poor and 1 very poor. Sorghum headed is at 70 percent, behind 1996 at 74 percent, but ahead of the five-year average at 45 percent. Sorghum coloring is at 10 percent, compared to 8 percent in 1996 and an average of 4 percent. Soybean condition is 10 percent excellent, 50 percent good, 34 percent fair, 5 percent poor and 1 percent very poor. Ninety-two percent of the soybean crop is blooming, the same as 1996 and ahead of the average of 81 percent. Statewide, 75 percent of the crop is setting pods, compared to 56 percent in 1996 and 47 percent for the average. Condition of the sunflower crop is 7 percent excellent, 50 percent good, 30 percent fair, 9 percent poor, and 4 percent very poor. Sixty-five percent of the sunflower crop has begun to petal. In the Northwest district, 53 percent of the crop has begun to petal. Thirty-five percent of the crop has begun to bloom. In the Northwest district, only 7 percent of the crop has begun to bloom. Third cutting of alfalfa is 75 percent complete, compared to the previous year at 78 percentd 63 percent for the five-year average. Fourth cutting is 15 percent complete. Statewide, there were 4.5 days suitable for fieldwork during the week (see table 3). The major field activities this week were irrigating, working wheat stubble, and cutting alfalfa. Topsoil moisture is rated 8 percent very short, 31 percent short, 49 percent adequate, and 12 percent surplus. Subsoil moisture is rated 6 percent very short, 31 percent short, 61 percent adequate, and 2 percent surplus. Pasture condition for the State is rated 9 percent excellent, 43 percent good, 33 percent fair, 12 percent poor, and 3 percent very poor. Some cattle moving to market. Stock water supplies remain mostly adequate.
